c23Feature.application: Module counts, masks and admissible scalar constants
c23Feature.limit: Object definitions only; not constexpr functions or non-null pointer relocation tables
c23Feature.benefit: Compiler diagnostics and fewer value macros; no automatic speed claim

c23Feature.application: typeof/typeof_unqual and local object inference in generated helpers
c23Feature.limit: Public ABI remains explicitly typed; existing GCC extensions are not new optimization
c23Feature.benefit: Less type duplication and extension-specific glue

c23Feature.application: nodiscard on fallible admission, initialization and publication results
c23Feature.limit: Diagnostics only; not linear ownership or automatic cleanup
c23Feature.benefit: Catch accidental ignored results; explicit outcome protocol still required

c23Feature.application: ckd_mul/ckd_add for count times element size plus header
c23Feature.limit: Reject overflow before publication; never consume overflow output; SDK capability unqualified
c23Feature.benefit: Unify boundary overflow handling; checks remain charged

c23Feature.application: Atomics, TLS, alignment and static assertions remain foundational
c23Feature.limit: C23 does not create multicore ownership, lock freedom, GC roots or tail-call guarantees
c23Feature.benefit: Standard baseline only; SMP correctness needs separate proofs

c23Feature.application: Stable C declarations, per-module descriptor data and compiled common helpers
c23Feature.limit: Static const and inline are older mechanisms; C23 alone does not remove preprocessing
c23Feature.benefit: Actual token/parse work can disappear only after producer/consumer replacement

c23Boundary.consumer: Stable C23 ABI and module setup
c23Boundary.contract: Header surface independent of module counts; ModuleSpec data and mutable binding instances separate
c23Boundary.retirement: Retire count-controlled general header assembly only after all binding modes/consumers migrate
c23Boundary.added: Descriptor relocations, cold helper calls, controlled hot inlining and ABI rebuild
c23Boundary.proofLimit: Structural key law only; actual expanded tokens, C ABI/layout and setup parity remain open

c23Boundary.consumer: GC, continuation and native frame consumers
c23Boundary.contract: One semantic role/layout owner; admitted descriptor ABI binds code and roots
c23Boundary.retirement: Retire duplicate IFD/OFD/return layout emission after all consumers and old captured-frame users migrate
c23Boundary.proofLimit: Supported mathematical cursor family only; native pointer, compiler liveness, control and whole GC remain open

c23Boundary.producer: Gerbil phase programs and Gambit CompileContext
c23Boundary.contract: Share immutable construction program; fresh binding/mark/context overlays and owned mutable compiler state
c23Boundary.retirement: Retire whole-request global-state authority only after protected writers and effects migrate
c23Boundary.added: Instance construction, input validation, worker transfer and roots
c23Boundary.proofLimit: Model context witnesses and projection counterexample; actual writer/effect closure and same-VM SMP remain open

c23Boundary.producer: Phase-query outputs plus native action requests
c23Boundary.contract: Semantic, generated-C, native and link keys separate; commit exact complete snapshot atomically
c23Boundary.retirement: Retire whole-module completion as sole gate and direct file-existence acceptance after all clients migrate
c23Boundary.added: Trace validation, manifest commit and failure/cancel drain
c23Boundary.proofLimit: Existing bounded scheduler and conditional publication law; no full source refinement or speedup

c23Edge.contract: C23 constants plus explicit descriptors; no module-count-driven public header
Shared implementation once per ABI/tool profile; hot inline policy explicit
Interface and executable macro support ready; fresh session identities
Semantic -> GVM -> C -> native with independent complete inputs
Exact snapshot, success and group completeness
Code/descriptor lease survives captured users; native refinement open
